big: Rohan sent ₹80,000 to a fraudster at 4 pm. He called the cyber helpline within the hour. Part of the money was held before it could leave the system. Minutes made the difference.

lines: I shared my OTP before I understood what was happening. Is it too late?
Not yet. The first hour matters most. Call 1930, call your bank to block, save the proof and file the complaint online.

rows: Call 1930, the national cyber fraud helpline
Call your bank to block cards, UPI or the account
Save messages, screenshots and transaction details
File the complaint on the cybercrime portal
note: For problems with a listed company or a registered broker, you can also file on SEBI SCORES.

title: If it happens
stops: Report financial cyber fraud quickly on 1930
Waiting a few weeks makes no difference
Screenshots and transaction details help the complaint
Deleting the chat protects you from more fraud
caps: The helpline exists to act quickly, and speed can stop money leaving.
Delay lets the money move on, and it is then harder to trace.
Evidence helps the bank and police follow the money.
Deleting the chat destroys the proof. Save everything instead.

q: Meena realises she has paid a fraudster a few minutes ago. What is the first step?
opts: Wait to see whether the money comes back
Call the cyber helpline 1930 at once
Post about it on social media first
Pay the fraudster again to stop him
why: Waiting lets the money move on, and it gets harder to trace each hour.
Quick reporting can stop money from leaving the system, so calling 1930 comes first.
A post does not stop the money, and it may warn the fraudster.
Paying again only gives the fraudster more of her money.

q: Rohan shared his card details with a caller. What should he ask his bank to do?
opts: Raise the card limit for a few days
Send the card details to the caller
Block the card, and stop any misuse
Close his savings account at once
why: A higher limit would let a thief take much more.
Sending details to the caller repeats the original mistake.
Blocking the card at once stops a thief from using what Rohan shared.
Closing the account is too much and cuts off his own access.

q: What should Meena keep after a fraud?
opts: Nothing, so that she can try to forget it
Only the amount that she has lost
Only the name that the caller gave her
why: Forgetting it destroys the proof, and the complaint will be weaker.
The amount alone does not show who took it or how.
A name given by a fraudster is usually false and proves little.
Messages, numbers and receipts show what happened and help the complaint.

q: Dadi has a complaint against a registered broker who has not returned her securities. Where can she file it online?
why: SEBI SCORES is the online system for complaints against listed companies and intermediaries.
A social media group cannot act against a broker, so it is no remedy.
A shopping website has nothing to do with market complaints.
A grocer has no way of acting on a complaint against a broker.

pts: Act within the first hour. Call 1930, then your bank.
Block cards, UPI or accounts, and save every proof.
File on the cybercrime portal, and on SEBI SCORES for market complaints.
